title: Student identity is directly disclosed by submitted identifiers
description: The student, as source, sends student ID together with the assignment and course information. This directly reveals the student's identity to the receiving system and ties the submission to a specific person.
assumptions: The student ID is unique and identifies the student to the portal or institution.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree node definitions.

title: Submission contents and metadata can link the student across courses and submissions in transit
description: The flow carries a work file, student ID, course, and submission timestamp. Together these attributes can be used to link multiple submissions to the same student and correlate activity across courses or over time if observed in transit or via flow metadata.
assumptions: An observer of the flow or its metadata can access repeated transmissions or associated network/application metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transport or surrounding telemetry exposes payload or metadata sufficient for correlation; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Assignment payload and submission metadata may be exposed in transit
description: The assignment file, student ID, course, and submission timestamp are privacy-relevant data. If the transmission channel or intermediary logging is insufficiently protected, these data may be disclosed during transit.
assumptions: Transport protection, endpoint validation, or intermediary handling may be inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on actual transport protections such as TLS and logging configuration; tree node is approximate.

title: Portal can link assignment submissions to the student's broader academic activity
description: On receipt, the Grades Portal Web App can associate the submitted assignment, student ID, course, and timestamp with other portal records, enabling linkage of the student's behavior and performance across courses and over time.
assumptions: The portal stores or has access to other records keyed by student identity or account.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side linkage risk, but the exact tree node is best-effort.

title: Portal can infer study patterns and behavior from submission metadata
description: The receiving application can derive personal information such as working habits, lateness, course participation, and activity patterns from the submission timestamp, course context, and file contents.
assumptions: The portal retains and analyzes submission metadata or makes it available to staff or analytics components.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node is approximate because detailed threat-tree nodes were not provided in context.

title: Portal may process assignment and identity data beyond the student's expectations or valid consent basis
description: The destination receives a work file plus identifying and contextual data. If the portal reuses these data for secondary purposes such as analytics, plagiarism-model training, profiling, or retention beyond what was communicated, the processing may be non-compliant with consent, transparency, or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Secondary use, excessive retention, or insufficient notice/consent is possible in the portal's processing.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as a potential compliance threat at the destination; applicability depends on actual notices, legal basis, and retention practices. Tree node is approximate.

title: Portal shares more personal data than strictly necessary with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. If all of these attributes are not strictly required for each submission or grading operation, the source process causes avoidable disclosure of personal data across an internal boundary, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes some requests could be fulfilled with fewer attributes, pseudonymous identifiers, or scoped tokens instead of the full set listed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for explicit, unnecessary disclosure/minimization; retrieved context did not provide a more specific Dd node for this exact case.

title: Data flow contains direct identifiers for the student
description: The routed request includes a student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone able to observe or access this flow can identify which student the submission or grading request concerns.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is unique within the institution or service ecosystem.

title: Assignment service processes identified student data
description: The destination service receives and processes identified data, including student id together with course and role context. This means the service operates on directly identified student records rather than anonymous or effectively pseudonymous data.
assumptions: Assumes P2 uses the received student id in its business logic or storage.

title: Submission and grading requests can link student activity across courses or actions
description: Combining student id with course and requesting role in the same flow enables correlation of multiple requests to the same student and role context over time. Observers or downstream processors could link submission and grading events across interactions, building a richer profile of academic activity.
assumptions: Assumes repeated requests use the same student identifier and are observable or retained in a correlatable form.
uncertainty_note: Specific L tree node id is inferred from standard LINDDUN linkability structure; exact node citation may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Received request data may enable profiling of a student's academic activities
description: At the destination, the combination of student id, course, file reference, and requesting role can reveal or support inference about a student's coursework, submissions, and grading interactions. If P2 stores or analyzes these requests beyond what is necessary, it can detect sensitive patterns about academic behavior.
assumptions: Assumes P2 logs, stores, aggregates, or analyzes request attributes beyond transient routing needs.
uncertainty_note: Specific D tree node id is based on best judgement for detectability/inference from received request data; exact node citation may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Excessive personal data stored with submission
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for the storage purpose, the act of sending them to the assignment store creates avoidable disclosure through over-collection/over-storage.
assumptions: Assumes the assignment store does not need the full set of attributes in identifiable form for every use case, or that some fields could be minimized, separated, or pseudonymized.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as best-fit minimality/explicit disclosure node; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Submission metadata enables linking of student activities
description: The data flow carries student id, course, and submission time alongside the assignment file. This combination can link multiple submissions and academic activities to the same student across courses or over time, especially if observed in transit or logged as flow metadata.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers and timestamps are visible in transit, middleware, or logs and can be correlated across events.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node is best-effort; applicability depends on whether transport/logging exposes these metadata beyond the immediate endpoints.

title: Student identity is directly exposed in transit
description: Because the flow includes a student id with the assignment and related metadata, any party able to observe the transmission can identify the submitting student directly.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is directly identifying or readily resolvable to a student by observers with ordinary system context.
uncertainty_note: If the channel is strongly protected and the identifier is pseudonymous outside the service boundary, likelihood would be lower.

title: Stored submission package may disclose more personal data than necessary
description: On receipt, the assignment store may retain the full assignment file plus student id, course, and exact submission time in one record. Keeping all fields together and indefinitely can create avoidable disclosure risk if some data could be reduced, separated, or retained for a shorter period.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores these attributes persistently and that not all are necessary at full granularity for all downstream purposes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure/minimality node; exact sub-node may differ across threat-tree editions.

title: Assignment records can be linked across contexts inside the store
description: The assignment store receives stable student identifiers, course information, and timestamps, enabling correlation of a student's submissions across assignments, courses, or terms if records are queried or combined.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 supports querying or aggregation across stored records and uses a stable student identifier.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is a genuine concern here, though the exact node id is selected by best judgement.

title: Stored submission metadata enables profiling of student behavior
description: Persistent storage of course and submission time together with identity can reveal behavioral patterns such as punctuality, workload, course participation, or study habits. This allows inference of personal characteristics beyond the immediate grading purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 data are retained long enough and accessible for analytics or secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Detectability/inference boundary can vary by methodology wording; selected as a best-fit detectability-related inference node.

title: Teacher submits identified account credentials and role context
description: When logging in and requesting the review queue, the teacher sends identified data to the web app, such as username/email, authentication material, and implicit role/course affiliation. This directly identifies the teacher to the system.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes account identifiers or credentials tied to a specific teacher account.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: Even if payload contents are protected, repeated requests on this flow can expose linkable metadata such as source IP, device/browser fingerprint, timing, and the fact that the same authenticated teacher is accessing grading functions for particular courses. This can enable linking of multiple actions to the same teacher.
assumptions: Assumes normal web/network metadata is observable within the system stack or by intermediaries handling the request.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate because the retrieved context did not include specific linkability subnodes.

title: Data in transit identifies the teacher to the receiving system
description: The flow carries identifiers or authentication tokens that allow the destination to recognize the teacher account making the request. If exposed in transit or logs, these data identify the teacher.
assumptions: Assumes the request contains session cookies, bearer tokens, usernames, or equivalent account-bound identifiers.

title: Portal can infer teaching workload and course-assignment patterns from queue requests
description: By receiving requests for submission-review queues, the portal can infer personal aspects of the teacher's professional activity, such as which courses they teach, when they grade, workload peaks, and responsiveness patterns. These inferences go beyond the bare login event.
assumptions: Assumes the application stores or analyzes request history by teacher and course.
uncertainty_note: Threat applies if request histories are retained or analyzed; exact tree-node citation is approximate due to limited retrieved tree context.

title: Portal may process login and activity data without sufficiently transparent notice
description: The web app may collect and use teacher login/request data for purposes such as monitoring, analytics, or retention without clearly informing the teacher at the point of collection, creating a transparency/compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notice, purpose specification, or just-in-time transparency for teacher activity data is incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible non-compliance threat, but it depends on organizational notice and policy details not provided; tree-node citation is approximate.

title: Portal discloses more student data to the teacher than necessary
description: The web app sends student names, work content, and submission times to the teacher. If the teacher does not need all of these attributes for the specific task, the source process causes avoidable disclosure of personal data by sharing more detail than is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes some displayed fields or level of detail may exceed what is strictly needed for the teacher's legitimate educational task.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality structure; exact subnode may differ in the canonical tree.

title: Student information could be exposed in transit to the teacher
description: This flow carries identifiable student data and submission content from the portal to the teacher. If the transmission channel or surrounding metadata is insufficiently protected, personal data may be disclosed to unintended parties during transfer.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may traverse networks or client-side contexts where interception, caching, or leakage via browser/network artifacts is possible.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on transport/session protections not specified in the prompt.

title: Teacher can link multiple submissions and timestamps to the same student
description: Because the flow includes student names together with work content and submission times, the transmitted data enables linking multiple records and activities to a specific student across assignments or over time.
assumptions: Assumes the portal presents repeated identifiers or stable names across multiple submissions.
uncertainty_note: This may be an intended functional property for teaching; listed as a privacy threat only insofar as the degree of linkability exceeds what is necessary.

title: Student identity is directly revealed to the teacher through the flow
description: The flow contains student names alongside submissions, making the student directly identifiable to the recipient. If anonymous or pseudonymous review would suffice in some contexts, this constitutes an identifiability threat.
assumptions: Assumes there are scenarios such as blind marking or preliminary review where direct identity is not strictly required.
uncertainty_note: If the teacher must know the student's identity for grading or safeguarding, this may be acceptable by design rather than a defect.

title: Teacher may infer additional sensitive information from submissions and timing
description: On receipt, the teacher can derive extra personal information from the student's work content and submission times, such as learning difficulties, health-related circumstances, behavioral patterns, or home situation. These inferences may go beyond what the student expected to disclose.
assumptions: Assumes submission content or timing patterns can reveal special-category or otherwise sensitive personal information.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; inference risk depends strongly on the nature of assignments and institutional context.

title: Teacher may process or further use submissions beyond the student's expectations
description: After receiving the submissions, the teacher could reuse, retain, or share the student names, work content, or timing information for purposes not transparent to the student, creating a non-compliance risk if this exceeds the stated educational purpose or legal basis.
assumptions: Assumes downstream handling by the teacher is not fully constrained by policy, training, or technical controls.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as a privacy threat at the destination because the prompt does not specify governance controls; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a grade/feedback entry
description: Because the teacher is the source of the grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id, insufficient binding of the submission to the teacher's authenticated identity or lack of trustworthy submission evidence could allow the teacher to repudiate having entered or changed the grade/feedback.
assumptions: Applies if the portal does not create tamper-evident audit records or strong attribution for grade submissions.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Grade submission flow can expose student or teacher identity in transit metadata
description: The transmitted payload contains student id and grader id, and transport metadata may also reveal communicating parties. If the flow is observable by unauthorized parties, the identities of the student and teacher involved in a grading event can be inferred.
assumptions: Applies if transport confidentiality/integrity protections or network access controls are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may vary depending on the project's threat-tree granularity.

title: Grade and feedback submissions may be linkable across events
description: Repeated submissions carrying stable identifiers such as student id and grader id can allow observers of the flow or intermediaries to link multiple grading events to the same teacher or student, building profiles of grading activity over time.
assumptions: Applies if identifiers are persistent and visible to parties beyond what is necessary, or if metadata is retained.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may differ; grounded in linkability via persistent identifiers and metadata.

title: Sensitive assignment performance information may be disclosed in transit
description: The flow carries a student's grade and written feedback, which are educational records and may contain sensitive personal information. Interception or unintended exposure of the flow would disclose the student's performance information and potentially the teacher's evaluative comments.
assumptions: Applies if encryption, endpoint validation, or secure channel protections are absent or weak.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may vary.

title: Portal may collect more grading-related personal data than necessary
description: On receipt, the web app may store or further process grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id in a way that exceeds what is necessary for grading, such as retaining excessive history, duplicating identifiers, or using free-text feedback for secondary analytics.
assumptions: Applies if the portal lacks data minimization controls, purpose limitation, or retention limits.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may differ; threat depends on downstream processing design.

title: Teacher may be unaware of secondary use or retention of submitted grading data
description: After receiving the submission, the portal may process or retain grades, feedback text, and identifiers for purposes not transparent to the teacher, such as analytics, model training, monitoring, or extended retention, leaving the teacher insufficiently informed about how the personal data is used.
assumptions: Applies if notices, UI cues, or policies do not clearly explain processing purposes and retention.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may vary.

title: Portal may process grading data without an appropriate legal basis or policy justification
description: The destination process receives student educational data and teacher identifiers. If the portal uses or stores this data beyond the legitimate grading purpose without a valid legal basis, contractual necessity, or institutional policy authorization, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applies if governance, policy mapping, or legal basis documentation for the processing is missing or inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and institutional context; exact subnode may differ.

title: Grade record content enables linkage across courses and assessments
description: When the grading service writes records containing student id, course, grade, grader id, and timestamp, it creates a persistent combination of identifiers and event data that can be linked across multiple submissions, courses, and grading events for the same student and grader.
assumptions: DS2 stores records over time and permits querying or later combination of records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicability by threat type/position but not detailed node mappings.

title: Student and grader are identifiable from written grade records
description: The grading service writes direct identifiers and quasi-identifiers, notably student id and grader id, together with course and timestamp. This makes the involved individuals identifiable in the stored record and in any copies derived from it.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are unique or readily resolvable to individuals.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Writing detailed feedback and grades may disclose sensitive academic information
description: The flow includes grade and feedback, which can reveal academic performance, weaknesses, accommodations, misconduct concerns, or other sensitive educational information about the student. Sending this full record to the database increases disclosure risk if not strictly necessary for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Feedback may contain free text and potentially sensitive remarks beyond the minimum needed for recordkeeping.
uncertainty_note: Specific node id is approximate; disclosure applicability is strong.

title: Database storage may enable excessive accumulation of grade history
description: On receipt, the grade records database may retain grade records, feedback, grader identifiers, and timestamps longer than necessary or in more detail than needed, creating a risk of unnecessary data accumulation and expanded exposure over time.
assumptions: Retention limits, minimization, or archival/deletion controls may be absent or weak.
uncertainty_note: Specific node id is approximate.

title: Secondary use of grade records beyond grading and recordkeeping
description: Once stored in the database, grade records could be repurposed for staff performance monitoring, student profiling, analytics, disciplinary review, or model training without being compatible with the original grading purpose or the expectations of students and graders.
assumptions: DS2 may be accessible to downstream reporting, analytics, or administrative functions.
uncertainty_note: Specific node id is approximate.

title: Storage of grades and feedback may occur without adequate transparency or legal basis
description: Persisting identifiable grade records with feedback, grader id, and timestamps in the database may require clear notice, defined retention, access governance, and an appropriate legal basis or policy justification. If these are missing or unclear, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy rules require purpose limitation, transparency, minimization, and retention governance.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and institutional policy; node id is approximate.

title: Students or graders may be unaware that detailed grading metadata is being persisted
description: By writing grader id and timestamp alongside grades and feedback, the service may process more metadata than data subjects expect. If this persistence is not adequately communicated, individuals may be unaware of the collection and storage of these details.
assumptions: Notices or UI cues may not clearly explain that grader identity and timestamps are stored with each grade record.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as unawareness/non-transparency rather than classic repudiation; LINDDUN uses Nr for non-repudiation, but some methodologies treat awareness/transparency separately. Included with moderate confidence only.

title: Student request contains identified data
description: To request grades and feedback, the student typically submits identifiers such as login credentials, session identifiers, student number, or account-linked request data. This means the source shares identified or directly attributable data with the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal requires authenticated access and the request is tied to a specific student account.

title: Request metadata can link repeated grade-access events to the same student
description: Even if the request payload is minimal, flow metadata such as IP address, device/browser fingerprint, session cookie, timing, and repeated access patterns can allow linking multiple requests to the same student and correlating them with other portal activity.
assumptions: Assumes normal web transport exposes routable network metadata and the application uses persistent sessions or similar request correlation mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed linkability subnodes.

title: Data in transit identifies the student to intermediaries or observers
description: The request flow may carry identifiers in headers, cookies, tokens, URLs, or payload fields that identify the student. If exposed to intermediaries, logs, or network observers, the student can be identified from the transmitted data.
assumptions: Assumes the request includes account/session identifiers or other student-specific attributes.

title: Portal can detect that the student is checking grades and feedback
description: By receiving this request, the web app learns that a particular student accessed the grades function at a specific time, potentially revealing behavior such as monitoring academic performance, reacting to assessment releases, or engagement patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the portal logs or can otherwise observe feature usage per authenticated student.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed detectability subnodes.

title: Portal may use the request for purposes beyond grade retrieval
description: The destination process may collect and reuse request data and access logs for analytics, profiling, monitoring, or secondary operational purposes that are not necessary for fulfilling the student's immediate request to view grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the portal or its operators retain request logs or telemetry beyond what is strictly necessary to serve the request.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed unawareness subnodes.

title: Insufficient transparency or legal basis for processing the request data
description: If the portal does not clearly inform students about what request data, identifiers, logs, and telemetry are processed when they access grades and feedback, or lacks an appropriate legal basis/governance for such processing, the handling of this flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy obligations require notice, purpose limitation, minimization, retention control, and lawful processing for student data.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction, institutional policies, and actual notices/controls; tree node is best-effort because detailed non-compliance subnodes were not provided.

title: Excessive disclosure of academic performance data
description: The portal process may disclose more grade or feedback information than necessary to fulfill the student's immediate purpose, such as showing historical grades, internal teacher remarks, or data about other assessments beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Assumes the UI or backend may return broader academic records or richer feedback than strictly needed for the viewing context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is based on best-fit LINDDUN disclosure categorization; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Student identifiable through grade and feedback content
description: The grades and teacher feedback are directly tied to an identifiable student. By sending this content, the process exposes identity-related personal data to whoever can access the receiving endpoint or screen.
assumptions: Assumes the displayed record is associated with a named or otherwise identifiable student account.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent to personalized grade delivery, but whether this is a threat depends on access-control context.

title: Interception of grades or feedback in transit
description: If the flow is insufficiently protected in transit, grades and teacher feedback could be observed by network attackers, browser extensions, shared-device malware, or intermediary infrastructure, revealing sensitive educational data.
assumptions: Assumes transport/session protections could be weak or bypassed in some deployment scenarios.
uncertainty_note: Applies strongly if transport confidentiality is not robust; if HTTPS with sound endpoint security is enforced, likelihood decreases.

title: Linkability via portal access metadata
description: Metadata on this flow, such as repeated access timing, session identifiers, IP address, device fingerprints, or course-specific URL patterns, could allow linking multiple grade-view events to the same student or household over time.
assumptions: Assumes network/application metadata is observable by the service, intermediaries, or third parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node; exact subnode may differ across LINDDUN Pro editions.

title: Disclosure through browser or intermediary caching
description: Responses containing grades and feedback may be cached in browsers, proxies, or content-delivery layers, enabling later unauthorized viewing on shared devices or by administrators of intermediary systems.
assumptions: Assumes cache-control headers or application behavior are not sufficiently restrictive for sensitive educational content.
uncertainty_note: Modeled at the flow because the risk stems from transmission artifacts and response handling in transit/storage layers.

title: Shoulder surfing or local exposure at the student's endpoint
description: Once displayed, grades and feedback may be exposed to nearby people, shared-device users, screen-recording software, or notification/previews on the student's device, causing unintended disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the student may access the portal from shared or observable environments.
uncertainty_note: Placed at destination because the disclosure arises from receipt/display at the student's endpoint rather than system-side sharing alone.

title: Student can deny having received or viewed grades/feedback
description: If the system lacks reliable evidence of delivery or access, the student may later dispute having seen a grade publication or teacher feedback, undermining accountability around notifications and acknowledgements.
assumptions: Assumes the organization relies on portal display as evidence that information was communicated.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is only relevant if proof of receipt/viewing matters in this educational process.

title: Insufficient transparency about grade/feedback disclosure
description: The portal may fail to clearly inform the student about what grade-related data is shown, its source, when it was updated, who authored feedback, or whether access/view events are logged, reducing transparency and informed expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not adequately explain data provenance, logging, or processing context.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on applicable transparency obligations and institutional policy.

title: Parent submits identified account credentials and child-linked request
description: The parent initiates login and a grades request using an account that is explicitly linked to a specific child. This causes identified data about the parent and the child relationship to be disclosed to the portal.
assumptions: The login/request includes account identifiers or credentials that uniquely identify the parent account and its linkage to a child account.

title: Login/request traffic can link parent and child identities in transit metadata
description: Even if payload contents are protected, the request flow may expose metadata that links a specific parent session or account to a specific child-record access event, enabling correlation of family relationship and educational-interest patterns.
assumptions: Observable metadata exists on the flow, such as stable account/session identifiers, request URLs, timing, or network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode for linkability via flow metadata was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Portal learns the parent-child relationship and grade-access intent
description: On receipt of the login and grades request, the portal can determine that this identified parent is associated with a particular child and is requesting that child's grades. This reveals personal and relational information beyond mere authentication.
assumptions: The portal processes the request in a way that makes the parent-child linkage and requested student record visible to application logic or logs.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subnode for inferring relationship/intent was not in the retrieved context.

title: Portal can detect and profile grade-checking behavior
description: By receiving the request, the portal can observe when and how often a parent checks a child's grades, enabling profiling of behavior and interests over time.
assumptions: The portal retains request events, timestamps, or analytics sufficient to observe recurring behavior.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability subnode is approximate because the retrieved context did not include the U threat tree.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for processing parent-child linkage and access logs
description: If the portal does not clearly inform the parent how login data, parent-child linkage, and grade-access events are processed, retained, or shared, the collection and use of this flow may occur without adequate awareness or valid consent/legal basis.
assumptions: Applicable notice/consent or other transparency obligations exist for this educational portal and are not fully satisfied.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the portal's actual notices, legal basis, and jurisdiction; exact non-compliance subnode is approximate.

title: Portal discloses detailed student performance data to the wrong parent account
description: The web app shares the child's grades, teacher feedback, and submission history with a parent. If account-to-student binding, session handling, or authorization checks are incorrect, the process may disclose a child's educational records to an unauthorized parent or guardian.
assumptions: Assumes the portal contains personally identifiable educational records and that parent access depends on application-level authorization and relationship mapping.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only provided applicable threat types/positions, not detailed node mappings.

title: Data in transit can identify the child and parent relationship
description: The flow carries grades, feedback, and submission history from the portal to the parent. If transport protection is weak or metadata is exposed, the content and associated identifiers can reveal the child's identity and the fact that EE2 is linked to that child as a parent.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted content or accompanying metadata includes names, student identifiers, class/course context, or account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Applies especially if TLS, caching controls, or URL/query-string handling are inadequate; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Repeated portal responses enable linkage of a parent's activity to a specific child profile
description: Even if some identifiers are minimized, repeated access patterns, stable resource identifiers, or consistent metadata in the flow can allow observers or intermediaries to link multiple interactions to the same child and parent over time.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers, URLs, cookies, or traffic patterns are observable by parties beyond the intended endpoints.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine risk mainly where network metadata, browser artifacts, or persistent identifiers are exposed.

title: Parent can retain or further share more educational history than necessary
description: Once received, the parent may store screenshots, downloads, or copied feedback/submission history indefinitely or share it onward, causing excessive dissemination of the child's educational data beyond the immediate purpose of viewing progress.
assumptions: Assumes the destination includes a user-controlled device/browser environment where content can be saved, copied, or redistributed.
uncertainty_note: This models disclosure arising at the destination because the recipient can further expose the data after receipt; exact node id is approximate.

title: Parent may be unaware of the extent of educational data revealed in the portal view
description: The destination may receive not only current grades but also detailed feedback and submission history. If the portal does not clearly communicate what categories of student data are shown and why, the disclosure may lack sufficient transparency and informed expectation for the recipient and, indirectly, the student.
assumptions: Assumes the UI does not clearly explain scope, purpose, or retention of the displayed records.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends strongly on applicable education/privacy law and portal notices; included as a plausible transparency risk rather than a certain violation.

title: Administrator submission directly identifies students, parents, and staff
description: The administrator sends names, email addresses, roles, and parent-child relationships to the portal. This act of disclosure from the source directly identifies multiple data subjects and associates them with account-management events.
assumptions: The submitted records contain real-world identifiers rather than pseudonyms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Parent-child links enable linkage of separate identities into family profiles
description: By creating or modifying parent-child links, the administrator causes distinct accounts to become linkable as members of the same family. This can reveal household composition and relationships that were previously separate.
assumptions: The portal stores or uses the relationship links in a way that makes the accounts associated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; linkage clearly applies, but exact node id may differ in the full LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Account-management updates disclose role and relationship attributes
description: The administrator's updates disclose personal attributes such as whether a person is a parent, child, student, or administrator, and disclose family relationship status through the parent-child link data.
assumptions: Roles and relationships are personal attributes in scope for privacy analysis.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate due to missing detailed node list in context.

title: Identifiers in transit can expose the identities of affected users
description: Names, email addresses, and relationship data traversing DF12 can identify the involved students, parents, and staff if intercepted or logged on the communication path.
assumptions: The flow may be observable through network interception, intermediary logging, browser tooling, or reverse proxies.
uncertainty_note: Applies especially if transport protection or logging controls are weak; exact tree node id is best-effort.

title: Relationship metadata in transit can link accounts and family members
description: Even while in transit, the payload structure and relationship fields can reveal which parent account is linked to which child account, enabling linkage between otherwise separate identities.
assumptions: Relationship identifiers or paired records are transmitted together or are inferable from request contents.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate.

title: Portal can aggregate accounts into family and role-based profiles

This enables linkage between student and parent accounts and potentially across classes or services if the directory is reused broadly.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 stores records in a way that permits cross-record correlation and is used by more than one function or context.

description: Account records in DS3 are likely to contain direct identifiers or stable account identifiers, and the parent-child links further narrow identity. On receipt and storage, DS3 may therefore make students and parents identifiable to parties with access to the directory.

description: Even if some identifiers are masked elsewhere, storing parent-child links in DS3 reveals that specific individuals are related and associated with the grading service. This exposes personal facts about family structure and participation in the educational context.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is accessible to administrators, integrated services, or other actors beyond the immediate grading function.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure/threat boundary between Detectability and Data Disclosure can be context-sensitive; here Detectability is used for revelation of personal facts from stored records.

description: Persisting parent-child relationship links and account records in DS3 may violate privacy requirements if the directory stores more data than necessary, retains it too long, or uses it for purposes beyond grading/account administration. description: Once received, the cloud hosting provider may be able to access, inspect, retain, or reuse the replicated grade records, assignments, and account directory beyond what data subjects expect. Receipt and storage by the destination creates a disclosure risk to a known third party, especially if provider-side administrative access, support access, or secondary processing is possible.
assumptions: Assumes provider personnel or provider-controlled systems can access plaintext or otherwise intelligible backup contents.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is approximate; grounded in destination-side disclosure to/processing by a third party.

title: Backup transfer may disclose sensitive records in transit
description: The nightly replication flow carries complete educational records and account-directory data across a boundary to the cloud provider. If the transfer channel, replication mechanism, or associated storage snapshots are insufficiently protected, the data may be exposed in transit or through intermediary infrastructure, causing avoidable disclosure of highly sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the replication traverses networks or intermediary infrastructure where interception, logging, or misdelivery is possible.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; this is a flow-centric disclosure threat focused on transfer exposure.

title: Full replicated dataset enables cross-context linkage at the provider
description: Combining full grade records, assignment content, and the account directory in one replicated backup gives the recipient and any systems handling the flow a rich basis to link identities, courses, performance, and activity across contexts. Even if each dataset has a legitimate operational purpose, their aggregation in a single transfer increases linkability of data subjects.

title: Replicated account directory and grade data can identify individuals at the provider

assumptions: Assumes the account directory contains direct identifiers or readily reversible identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; the threat clearly concerns destination-side identifiability enabled by included identifiers.

title: Secondary hosting/backup use may exceed data subjects' consent or reasonable expectations
description: Data subjects may have provided educational data for teaching, grading, and account administration, but not reasonably expect full records to be replicated to a third-party hosting provider in identifiable form. If this transfer or the provider's subsequent handling is not covered by an appropriate legal basis, notice, or consent framework, the flow creates a non-compliance threat.

description: The grade records database may provide more grade-related personal data than is necessary for the specific view being built. Because the same read supports student, parent, and teacher views, DS2 may disclose full records, historical grades, comments, or identifiers beyond what P2 needs for a given request, increasing unnecessary exposure of student data.

This can make separate role contexts linkable through shared identifiers or combined datasets.

description: Processing full grade records in P2 to build multiple audience-specific views may violate obligations such as purpose limitation, data minimization, access control, retention limits, or role-based disclosure restrictions if the service retrieves or uses more data than necessary.
